easy.def: A word that shows something is inside or within.
examples: The milk is in the fridge.
We swim in the pool.
I was born in May.

more.def: A word used to show that something is inside a place, a shape, a group, or a time.
examples: The fish swim in the deep part of the lake.
Our class stood in a circle.
Leaves turn red and gold in autumn.

easy.def: Not being able to do something.
examples: His inability to swim.
The inability to see.
Her inability to run.

more.def: The state of not being able to do something.
examples: His inability to swim kept him out of the deep water.
The team's inability to score cost them the game.
Her inability to find the keys made her late.

easy.def: Not right for the time or place.
examples: Shouting is inappropriate in the library.
The joke was inappropriate.
That is inappropriate.

more.def: Not suitable for the time or place, or not proper.
examples: Loud talk is inappropriate in a library.
The joke was inappropriate for school.
Wearing sandals was inappropriate for the hike.

easy.def: A stick or powder that smells sweet when it burns.
examples: The temple smelled of incense.
Incense smells sweet.
They burned incense.

more.def: A substance that gives off a sweet smell when it is burned, often used in religious ceremonies.
examples: The temple smelled of sweet incense.
A stick of incense burned in a holder on the shelf.
People burn incense in many parts of the world.

easy.def: A small unit for measuring how long something is.
examples: The bug is one inch long.
My pencil is six inches.
The snow was an inch deep.

more.def: A small unit of length. Twelve of them make a foot.
examples: The beetle was about an inch long.
A ruler is twelve inches long.
Three inches of snow fell overnight.

easy.def: Something that happens.
examples: The incident was short.
An odd incident happened at school.
He told us about the incident.

more.def: Something that happens, especially something unusual or surprising.
examples: A strange incident happened at lunch when the cat walked in.
The teacher wrote down the incident in her notes.
There was a small incident on the bus.

easy.def: Happening as a small extra thing.
examples: An incidental cost.
The noise was incidental.
The incidental music played.

more.def: Happening as a minor part of something else.
examples: There is an incidental cost for the bag.
The incidental music in the movie was soft.
An incidental detail did not matter.

easy.def: By the way.
examples: Incidentally, I saw your friend today.
Incidentally, it is my birthday.
He said, "Incidentally, we have no milk."

more.def: Used to add a side comment to what you are saying.
examples: Incidentally, I saw your cousin at the store today.
We are going to the park, and, incidentally, it is a nice day.
The soup is ready and, incidentally, so is the bread.

easy.def: A slope.
examples: The cart rolled down the incline.
The incline is steep.
We climbed the incline.

more.def: A surface that slopes, like a ramp.
examples: The train slowed on the steep incline.
The road had a steep incline.
We pushed the wheelbarrow up the incline.

easy.def: Likely to do something.
examples: I am inclined to nap.
She is inclined to help.
He is not inclined to go.

more.def: Having a wish or tendency to do something.
examples: I am inclined to say yes.
She is inclined to help whenever she can.
He is not inclined to go out in the rain.

easy.def: To make someone or something a part of a group.
examples: Please include me in your game.
The lunch includes an apple.
We include everyone in our club.

more.def: To have as a part, or to make something part of a group.
examples: The price of the ticket includes a drink and a snack.
The tour includes a visit to the castle.
Be sure to include your name on your paper.

easy.def: Money that you earn.
examples: Her income is small.
Dad's income pays the bills.
The family has a good income.

more.def: The money that a person or family receives, usually from work.
examples: Her income comes from teaching.
Her income from the farm rose this year.
The family had a small income.

easy.def: Coming in.
examples: The incoming tide is high.
An incoming call.
The incoming mail is on the desk.

more.def: Coming in or arriving.
examples: The incoming tide covered the sand.
An incoming call rang on the phone.
The incoming class has thirty students.

easy.def: Not finished or not whole.
examples: The puzzle is incomplete.
An incomplete list.
The picture is incomplete.

more.def: Not finished, or missing some parts.
examples: The puzzle was incomplete because one piece was missing.
Her homework was incomplete, so she finished it after dinner.
The list of names is incomplete.

easy.def: Not thinking about how others feel.
examples: It is inconsiderate to be loud at night.
He was inconsiderate and took all the cake.
Do not be inconsiderate.

more.def: Not caring about the feelings or needs of other people.
examples: It was inconsiderate to play loud music while the baby slept.
The inconsiderate boy left his mess for others to clean.
She felt bad for being inconsiderate to her friend.

easy.def: Not always the same.
examples: His work is inconsistent.
The weather is inconsistent.
The team was inconsistent.

more.def: Not staying the same, or not matching other things.
examples: The inconsistent weather went from sunny to rainy.
Her answers were inconsistent, so we were not sure.
The team was inconsistent and won only some games.

easy.def: A small trouble.
examples: The delay was an inconvenience.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.
The rain was an inconvenience.

more.def: Something that causes a little trouble or makes things harder.
examples: The late bus was an inconvenience.
The detour was a minor inconvenience.
The closed road caused some inconvenience.

easy.def: Not easy or handy.
examples: It is inconvenient.
An inconvenient time.
The store is inconvenient.

more.def: Causing trouble or making things harder, because it is not handy or does not suit you.
examples: The bus stop is inconvenient because it is far from my house.
It was an inconvenient time for a phone call.
The long walk was inconvenient with heavy bags.

easy.def: Not right.
examples: The answer is incorrect.
An incorrect word.
My answer was incorrect.

more.def: Not correct, or not matching the facts or the rules.
examples: My answer on the math test was incorrect, so I fixed it.
The spelling of the word is incorrect.
The teacher showed us that our idea was incorrect.

easy.def: To get bigger.
examples: The price will increase.
The plant increased in size.
We increased the speed.

more.def: To become larger or to make something larger in amount or number.
examples: The price of milk will increase next month.
The plant increased in height every week.
She increased the volume on the radio.

easy.def: A rise in amount.
examples: There was an increase in price.
The increase is small.
An increase in rain.

more.def: A rise in size, amount or number.
examples: There was an increase in the price of gas.
The increase in snow made the roads slippery.
We saw an increase in visitors.

easy.def: Very hard to believe; amazing.
examples: The view was incredible.
It was an incredible jump.
What an incredible story!

more.def: So amazing or surprising that it is hard to believe.
examples: The view from the mountain was incredible.
She made an incredible jump.
The magician did an incredible trick.

easy.def: Extremely.
examples: The cake was incredibly good.
It was incredibly cold.
The tower is incredibly tall.

more.def: To a very great degree, in a way that is hard to believe.
examples: The mountain was incredibly steep.
It was incredibly cold last night.
The runner was incredibly fast.

easy.def: A warm box for hatching eggs or helping tiny babies.
examples: The eggs are in an incubator.
A baby chick came from the incubator.
The incubator is warm.

more.def: A warm, safe box used to hatch eggs or to keep very small, early babies warm.
examples: The chicks hatched in the incubator.
A tiny baby was kept warm in an incubator.
The eggs stayed in the incubator for three weeks.

easy.def: Really; for sure.
examples: It is indeed cold.
Yes, indeed!
Indeed, I am hungry.

more.def: Used to show that something is really true.
examples: It was indeed the best day of my life.
The test was hard indeed.
Yes, indeed, we are ready to go.

easy.def: Being free and able to do things yourself.
examples: She is learning independence.
The country won its independence.
A bike gives me independence.

more.def: The freedom to make your own choices and do things without help, or the freedom of a country to rule itself.
examples: She is learning independence by making her own lunch.
The country celebrated its independence with a parade.
A bike gave him the independence to ride to school by himself.

easy.def: Not needing others.
examples: I am independent.
She is an independent girl.
The independent boy tied his shoes.

more.def: Able to do things on your own, without help from others.
examples: I am independent now and tie my own shoes.
She is an independent thinker.
The country became independent after many years.

easy.def: Not able to be broken or ruined.
examples: The toy is nearly indestructible.
He thought his fort was indestructible.
A hero in the comic is indestructible.

more.def: Impossible to destroy, break or wear out.
examples: The superhero in the cartoon has an indestructible shield.
No toy is truly indestructible, even the strongest ones.
The scientists tested a nearly indestructible new plastic.

easy.def: A list at the back of a book that tells where to find things.
examples: I looked in the index.
The index lists words.
The book has an index.

more.def: An alphabetical list at the back of a book that tells you which pages to find things on.
examples: I looked up "volcano" in the index to find the right page.
The index of the book listed every animal in order.
Use the index to find the topic you need.

easy.def: To show or point to something.
examples: The arrow indicates the way.
The sign indicates the exit.
The light indicates that it is ready.

more.def: To show or point out something, or to be a sign of it.
examples: The arrow on the sign indicates which way to go.
Dark clouds indicate that rain may fall.
The light on the oven indicates that it is hot.

easy.def: Something that shows you what is happening.
examples: The gas indicator is low.
A light is an indicator.
The indicator shows the time.

more.def: A thing, such as a light or a dial, that shows what is going on.
examples: The fuel indicator showed the tank was nearly empty.
A red light is an indicator that the oven is on.
A rising temperature is an indicator of fever.

easy.def: Not caring about something.
examples: He showed indifference.
The cat's indifference was clear.
She greeted the news with indifference.

more.def: A lack of interest or concern.
examples: He shrugged with indifference when asked to choose.
The cat looked at the toy with indifference.
The class received the news with indifference.

easy.def: Not caring about something.
examples: He was indifferent to the game.
She seemed indifferent.
The cat was indifferent.

more.def: Not interested in something or not caring which happens.
examples: He seemed indifferent to the game and read a book.
The cat was indifferent to the new toy.
She was indifferent about which movie to see.

easy.def: A sore stomach after eating.
examples: I had indigestion.
Too much pizza gave me indigestion.
He has indigestion.

more.def: A sore or uncomfortable feeling in the stomach, caused by eating too much or too fast.
examples: I got indigestion from eating too much pizza.
He has indigestion when he eats too quickly.
The medicine helped her indigestion.

easy.def: A deep blue-purple color.
examples: Indigo is a color.
The sky turned indigo.
A deep indigo.

more.def: A deep blue color with a hint of purple, one of the colors of the rainbow.
examples: Indigo is the color between blue and violet in the rainbow.
The sky turned a deep indigo as night fell.
Her jeans were dyed indigo.

easy.def: One alone.
examples: Each individual cup has a lid.
The individual pieces fit together.
We got individual pizzas.

more.def: Single and separate from others, or meant for one person.
examples: Each child got an individual cup of juice.
The teacher gave individual help to each student.
Each snowflake has an individual shape.

easy.def: One person.
examples: Each individual has a name.
An individual can make a difference.
She is a strong individual.

more.def: One single person, as different from a group.
examples: Every individual has a different fingerprint.
One individual can make a difference.
She is a kind and thoughtful individual.

easy.def: What makes you different from everyone else.
examples: She shows her individuality.
Everyone has individuality.
His individuality shines.

more.def: The qualities that make a person different from everyone else.
examples: She shows her individuality through her clothes.
Each artist's individuality shows in the paintings.
Our teacher likes to see individuality in our writing.

easy.def: Inside a building.
examples: We play indoor games on a rainy day.
An indoor pool is warm.
I have an indoor cat.

more.def: Done or found inside a building.
examples: An indoor pool lets us swim all winter.
Rain meant we played indoor games all afternoon.
The indoor plants need light from the window.

easy.def: Inside a building.
examples: We played indoors.
Stay indoors when it rains.
Go indoors now.

more.def: Inside a building or house, not outside.
examples: We stayed indoors because of the thunderstorm.
The children played board games indoors on the rainy day.
Please come indoors and wash your hands.

easy.def: A treat you enjoy.
examples: A cookie is an indulgence.
Cake is an indulgence.
The ice cream was an indulgence.

more.def: Something that you enjoy and do not really need, or giving in to what someone wants.
examples: A big piece of cake was a sweet indulgence.
The grandparents' indulgence made the kids happy.
Chocolate is an indulgence for many people.

easy.def: Having to do with factories and big businesses.
examples: The industrial part of town has big factories.
We saw an industrial machine.
The industrial area is loud.

more.def: Having to do with factories and making things in large amounts.
examples: The industrial area of the city is full of factories and warehouses.
The industrial revolution brought machines into many workplaces.
A large industrial fan kept the factory cool.

easy.def: All the businesses that make one kind of thing.
examples: The car industry makes cars.
The toy industry is big.
The food industry feeds us.

more.def: All the companies and work that make a certain kind of thing or give a certain service.
examples: The car industry builds millions of cars each year.
Tourism is a big industry in the town.
The movie industry makes films.

easy.def: Sure to happen.
examples: Rain is inevitable.
Change is inevitable.
The end was inevitable.

more.def: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
examples: Rain was inevitable in the spring.
Change is inevitable as we grow up.
With the clouds above, a storm was inevitable.

easy.def: So bad it cannot be forgiven.
examples: It was inexcusable.
Hitting is inexcusable.
The rude behavior is inexcusable.

more.def: Too bad to be excused or forgiven.
examples: Being late without calling was inexcusable.
It is inexcusable to be rude to guests.
The inexcusable mistake cost us the game.

easy.def: Well known for being bad.
examples: The pirate was infamous.
An infamous thief.
He was infamous for tricks.

more.def: Well known for something bad or wrong, not for something good.
examples: The infamous pirate was known for stealing treasure from many ships.
The old road is infamous for its sharp, dangerous curves.
The fox was infamous in the village for stealing eggs.

easy.def: A very young baby.
examples: The infant slept.
An infant cries.
The infant is small.

more.def: A baby in its first year of life.
examples: The infant slept in her mother's arms.
An infant needs a lot of care.
The nurse held the tiny infant.

easy.def: To make someone sick with germs.
examples: Germs infect people.
The cut got infected.
A virus infected him.

more.def: To pass germs to a person, animal or plant so that it becomes sick.
examples: Germs can infect a cut.
The virus infected many people.
The cut became infected, and the doctor gave her medicine.

easy.def: A sickness caused by germs.
examples: I have an ear infection.
The cut got an infection.
The infection went away.

more.def: A sickness that is caused by germs entering the body.
examples: I had an ear infection and took medicine.
The cut developed an infection.
Washing your hands helps stop infection.

easy.def: Not as good as another.
examples: The old bike was inferior.
This toy is inferior to that one.
It tasted inferior.

more.def: Lower in quality, rank or value than something else.
examples: The cheap pen was inferior to the one I had before, and it leaked.
Nobody should be made to feel inferior to another person.
The inferior boots let in water on the very first day.

easy.def: A very big, hot fire.
examples: The house was an inferno.
The inferno was hot.
Firefighters fought the inferno.

more.def: A huge, fierce fire that burns out of control.
examples: Firefighters battled the inferno in the forest.
The barn became an inferno in minutes.
Smoke rose from the raging inferno.

easy.def: To fill a place with bugs or pests.
examples: Ants infest the kitchen.
Bugs infested the garden.
Rats can infest an old barn.

more.def: To be in a place in large numbers and cause trouble, as insects or pests do.
examples: Ants infested the picnic basket.
Termites infested the old wooden fence.
Weeds can infest a garden if they are not pulled.

easy.def: Without end.
examples: The sky seems infinite.
Space is infinite.
Her patience was infinite.

more.def: Having no end or limit.
examples: The night sky seems infinite.
Some people believe that space is infinite.
She had infinite patience with the little children.

easy.def: A number or space that never ends.
examples: Infinity never ends.
Count to infinity.
The sky seems like infinity.

more.def: Endless space, time or number that has no limit.
examples: The stars seem to stretch to infinity.
You can count numbers all day and never reach infinity.
The symbol for infinity looks like a figure eight on its side.

easy.def: To fill with air.
examples: Inflate the balloon.
He inflated the ball.
She will inflate the tire.

more.def: To fill something with air or gas so it gets bigger.
examples: Dad inflated the bike tire with a pump.
She inflated the balloon for the party.
He inflated the raft before the trip.

easy.def: To make someone suffer or put up with something unpleasant.
examples: The storm inflicted damage.
Do not inflict pain.
The loss inflicted sadness.

more.def: To cause something harmful or unpleasant to happen to someone.
examples: The storm inflicted damage on the town.
It is wrong to inflict pain on any animal.
The long, boring talk inflicted misery on the audience.

easy.def: The power to change someone or something.
examples: Friends have an influence on us.
The moon has an influence on the tides.
Her teacher was a good influence.

more.def: The power to change how someone thinks or acts, or to change how something happens.
examples: Friends can have a big influence on you.
The moon's influence causes the tides.
He was a good influence on his little brother.

easy.def: A short word for information.
examples: I need info on the trip.
Look up the info.
The sign has info.

more.def: A short, informal word for information.
examples: I need some info on the trip.
Look up the info about the museum on the web.
The sign had all the info we needed about the park.

easy.def: A long TV ad that gives lots of information.
examples: The infomercial was long.
I saw an infomercial.
The infomercial sells a mop.

more.def: A long TV advertisement that gives a lot of information about a product.
examples: Dad watched an infomercial about a new mop.
The infomercial lasted half an hour.
The infomercial showed how the gadget worked.

easy.def: To tell someone something.
examples: Please inform me when it is done.
The sign informs us of the rules.
She informed the teacher.

more.def: To tell someone a fact or a piece of news that they need or want to know.
examples: The coach informed the team that practice was canceled.
A bell informs the class that it is time for lunch.
Please inform us if you cannot come to the party.

easy.def: Relaxed and not formal.
examples: It is an informal party.
Informal clothes.
An informal talk.

more.def: Relaxed and not following strict rules, such as in an easy talk or a casual party.
examples: We held an informal party in the backyard with no fancy clothes.
She wrote an informal note to her friend.
In informal speech, people often say "gonna" for "going to."

easy.def: Facts about something.
examples: I need information about frogs.
The sign gives information.
Ask for information.

more.def: Facts or details about something.
examples: The library has information about every state.
Read the sign for information about the park.
I found information about frogs in a book.

easy.def: Very clever at thinking up new ideas.
examples: She made an ingenious plan.
An ingenious tool.
His idea was ingenious.

more.def: Very clever and good at coming up with new ways of doing things.
examples: She made an ingenious plan to carry all the books at once.
The ingenious inventor built a machine that could sort socks.
It was an ingenious way to keep the door open.

easy.def: One of the things used to make food.
examples: Flour is an ingredient.
Sugar is an ingredient in cake.
The recipe lists each ingredient.

more.def: One of the foods or things that you mix together to make a dish or other product.
examples: Eggs, flour and milk are the main ingredients in pancakes.
Mom read the list of ingredients on the recipe card.
Patience is an important ingredient for learning to play an instrument.

easy.def: A person or animal that lives in a place.
examples: The town has many inhabitants.
An owl is an inhabitant of the woods.
Each inhabitant has a home.

more.def: A person or animal that lives in a certain place.
examples: The island's only inhabitants were birds and seals.
Every inhabitant of the village came to the fair.
Ants are inhabitants of nearly every part of the world.

easy.def: To breathe in.
examples: Inhale slowly.
I inhale the fresh air.
She inhaled a deep breath.

more.def: To take air or another gas into your lungs.
examples: Inhale deeply through your nose and count to three.
She inhaled the sweet smell of the cookies baking.
Divers inhale air from tanks on their backs.

easy.def: A small device that people use to breathe in medicine.
examples: She used her inhaler.
The inhaler helps her breathe.
He carries an inhaler.

more.def: A small device that a person uses to breathe in medicine to help them breathe more easily.
examples: She used her inhaler before the race.
An inhaler helps people with asthma breathe more easily.
He keeps his inhaler in his backpack.

easy.def: To get something from a parent or someone who has died.
examples: I inherited my mom's eyes.
She inherited a ring.
He will inherit the farm.

more.def: To receive money or things from a person who has died, or to get a trait from your parents.
examples: I inherited my mother's curly hair.
She inherited her grandmother's ring.
He will inherit the farm one day.

easy.def: The first letter of a name.
examples: My initial is J.
The initials are on my backpack.
She wrote her initials.

more.def: The first letter of a person's name.
examples: My initials are on my backpack.
She signed with her initials.
The sign had the letters J.K. for his initials.

easy.def: First, at the start.
examples: The initial plan was simple.
My initial reaction was shock.
The initial step is easy.

more.def: Happening at the beginning.
examples: The initial plan was to leave at nine.
My initial thought was that it was a joke.
The initial step is to read the directions.

easy.def: At the start.
examples: Initially, I was scared.
He was shy initially.
I initially said no.

more.def: At the beginning, or in the first place.
examples: Initially, I was nervous, but then I began to have fun.
The plan was initially to go on Friday, but it changed.
She was shy initially but made friends quickly.

easy.def: To start.
examples: I initiate the game.
The teacher initiated the lesson.
She initiated the plan.

more.def: To begin something or get it going.
examples: The teacher initiated the new reading plan.
She initiated a recycling program at school.
Who will initiate the game?

easy.def: The act of beginning something or welcoming someone into a group.
examples: We had an initiation for the club.
The initiation was fun.
There is an initiation for new members.

more.def: The act of starting something, or a special event that welcomes someone into a group.
examples: The club held an initiation for its new members.
The initiation of the project took place in May.
Her initiation into the choir included singing a song.

easy.def: Doing something on your own without being told.
examples: She took the initiative and cleaned up.
He showed initiative.
Good initiative helps the team.

more.def: The ability or the willingness to start doing something yourself without waiting to be told.
examples: She showed initiative by cleaning up the classroom without being asked.
Tom took the initiative and called the whole team to a meeting.
The school started a new initiative to plant trees in the yard.

easy.def: To put medicine into the body with a needle.
examples: The nurse injects the medicine.
The doctor injected the shot.
She was injected.

more.def: To put medicine or liquid into the body using a needle.
examples: The nurse injected the medicine into my arm.
The doctor injects a vaccine.
He was injected against the flu.

easy.def: A shot of medicine.
examples: I got an injection.
The injection was quick.
The nurse gave an injection.

more.def: A dose of medicine that is put into the body through a needle.
examples: I got an injection at the doctor's office.
Insulin is given by injection.
The nurse gave an injection for the flu.

easy.def: To hurt someone or something.
examples: I injured my knee.
The fall injured her arm.
He injured his ankle.

more.def: To cause harm to a person or animal.
examples: I injured my knee playing soccer.
The fall injured her wrist.
The hawk had an injured wing.

easy.def: A hurt to the body.
examples: I have an injury.
His leg injury hurts.
The injury healed.

more.def: Damage to a part of the body, such as a cut or a broken bone.
examples: He had an injury to his ankle.
The nurse looked at my knee injury.
The injury healed after a few weeks.

easy.def: Something unfair.
examples: It was an injustice.
She spoke up about the injustice.
Injustice is wrong.

more.def: Something unfair that happens when people are not treated the way they should be.
examples: It was an injustice when only one child was punished.
She spoke up about the injustice at school.
People worked hard to stop injustice in the town.

easy.def: Colored liquid for writing.
examples: The pen has blue ink.
The ink is black.
I spilled ink.

more.def: A colored liquid that is used for writing or printing.
examples: The pen ran out of ink.
The ink stained my fingers blue.
The printer uses black ink.

easy.def: A small hotel.
examples: We stayed at an inn.
The inn is by the road.
The inn has six rooms.

more.def: A small hotel or a place where travelers can stay and eat.
examples: We stayed the night at a cozy inn.
The inn served hot soup.
The old inn sat beside the road.

easy.def: On the inside.
examples: The inner room is dark.
The inner layer is soft.
The inner circle.

more.def: Closer to the middle, or on the inside.
examples: The inner room has no windows.
The inner layer of the onion is soft.
The inner tube of the tire has a leak.

easy.def: One part of a baseball game.
examples: Baseball has nine innings.
It is the last inning.
We scored in the third inning.

more.def: One of the parts of a baseball game, in which each team gets a turn to bat.
examples: The game has nine innings.
We scored three runs in the last inning.
The pitcher threw for six innings.

easy.def: Not being guilty.
examples: He proved his innocence.
The child's innocence was clear.
The jury believed in his innocence.

more.def: The state of not having done anything wrong.
examples: He proved his innocence to the teacher.
The jury believed in her innocence.
The innocence of the child made everyone smile.

easy.def: Not having done anything wrong.
examples: The boy was innocent.
I am innocent.
The dog looked innocent.

more.def: Not guilty of a crime or wrongdoing; not having done what you are blamed for.
examples: The detective proved that the boy was innocent.
I am innocent because I did not touch the cookies.
The innocent dog sat quietly.

easy.def: What you put into a computer.
examples: Type your input.
The input was wrong.
The computer needs input.

more.def: Information, ideas or advice that is given to a person or put into a computer.
examples: The computer needs input before it can give an answer.
The teacher asked for our input on where to go for the class trip.
Typing numbers on the keyboard is one kind of input.

easy.def: To ask about something.
examples: I inquire at the desk.
She inquired about the price.
He inquired about the bus.

more.def: To ask a question to get information.
examples: I inquired at the desk about the lost mittens.
She inquired about the price of the book.
He inquired when the next bus would come.

easy.def: A question or a careful search for facts.
examples: I made an inquiry at the desk.
The inquiry took a week.
Her inquiry was polite.

more.def: A question that you ask to get information, or a careful search to find out the facts about something.
examples: I made an inquiry at the front desk about the opening time.
The school began an inquiry into how the window got broken.
A polite inquiry to the librarian helped me find the book.

easy.def: Always asking questions and wanting to learn.
examples: The inquisitive child asked why.
An inquisitive kitten.
She is inquisitive.

more.def: Always asking questions and eager to find out new things.
examples: The inquisitive child asked why the sky was blue and where the wind came from.
An inquisitive kitten explored every corner of the room.
The inquisitive scientist looked at everything through a magnifying glass.

easy.def: Very silly or wild.
examples: That idea is insane.
An insane amount of snow.
The ride was insane.

more.def: Very wild or extreme. In its medical meaning, it should be used carefully.
examples: The amount of snow was insane.
That roller coaster is insane.
It is an insane plan to cross the river on a log.

easy.def: To write or carve words on something.
examples: They inscribe names on it.
The ring was inscribed.
The artist inscribed a name.

more.def: To write or carve words onto a surface so they last.
examples: They inscribed our names on the trophy.
The ring was inscribed with a date.
Grandpa inscribed his name inside the book.

easy.def: Words that are cut or written on something hard.
examples: The statue has an inscription.
I read the inscription on the ring.
An inscription is on the stone.

more.def: Words that are carved or written on a hard thing, such as a stone, a coin or a ring.
examples: The inscription on the old stone told the name of the town's founder.
She read the inscription inside the ring: "Love, Grandma."
Words in an old language were carved as an inscription on the wall.

easy.def: A small bug with six legs.
examples: An ant is an insect.
A bee is an insect that can sting.
The insect sat on a leaf.

more.def: A small animal with six legs and a body in three parts, often with wings.
examples: Bees, ants, and butterflies are all insects.
Some insects, like crickets, make sounds with their wings.
An insect's body has three main parts.

easy.def: Not feeling sure of yourself.
examples: He felt insecure about the new school.
She was insecure.
I feel insecure on stage.

more.def: Not confident, or worried that you are not good enough.
examples: He felt insecure on his first day at the new school.
She was insecure about reading aloud.
I feel insecure when I do not know the answer.

easy.def: Not safe or firmly fixed.
examples: The ladder is insecure.
The gate is insecure.
The old bridge is insecure.

more.def: Not safe or not held firmly in place.
examples: The ladder was insecure and wobbled when I climbed it.
An insecure fence let the dog run away.
The bridge looked old and insecure.

easy.def: Not feeling safe or sure of yourself.
examples: She felt insecurity.
Insecurity is hard.
His insecurity grew.

more.def: A feeling of not being sure of yourself or not feeling safe.
examples: She felt insecurity on her first day at the new school.
Everyone has some insecurity, and it is okay to ask for help.
His insecurity made him afraid to speak up.

easy.def: Not caring about other people's feelings.
examples: It was insensitive to laugh.
He was insensitive.
The insensitive comment hurt.

more.def: Not thinking about or caring for other people's feelings.
examples: It was insensitive to laugh when she dropped her tray.
His insensitive comment hurt his friend.
She apologized for being insensitive.

easy.def: Always together.
examples: The two friends are inseparable.
The twins are inseparable.
They are inseparable pals.

more.def: Always together and never apart, or unable to be parted.
examples: The two friends were inseparable all summer.
The twins are inseparable and do everything together.
The dog and the boy were inseparable.

easy.def: To put something into something else.
examples: Insert the key in the lock.
I insert a coin.
She inserted a card.

more.def: To put one thing inside another.
examples: Insert the key into the lock and turn it.
She inserted a new battery into the toy.
He inserted a picture in the middle of his report.

easy.def: In the inner part of something.
examples: The cat is inside the box.
Look inside the bag.
We stayed inside the tent.

more.def: In or into the inner part of something.
examples: There is a surprise inside the small box.
The kitten curled up inside my coat.
He kept the secret inside his heart.

easy.def: In a house or building.
examples: Let us go inside.
We play inside.
It is cold, so stay inside.

more.def: Into or within a house or other building.
examples: It started to rain, so we went inside.
The dog barked until we let him inside.
We stayed inside all day because of the snow.

easy.def: A clear idea about what something really means.
examples: She had an insight.
The book gave me insight.
He had a good insight.

more.def: A deep understanding of something, or a clear idea of how it works.
examples: The book gave me insight into how bees live.
She had an insight that helped her solve the puzzle.
Talking to my grandfather gave me insight into what school was like long ago.

easy.def: Showing deep understanding.
examples: That is an insightful idea.
She gave an insightful answer.
I saw an insightful girl.

more.def: Showing a deep and clear understanding of something.
examples: She gave an insightful answer to the question.
The insightful teacher saw why the boy was upset.
His insightful comment helped the class.

easy.def: To say something strongly.
examples: I insist on helping.
She insisted on paying.
He insists he is right.

more.def: To say firmly that something must be done or is true.
examples: I insist that you take the last piece.
She insisted on helping with the dishes.
He insists that he saw a fox.

easy.def: Keeping on asking until you get it.
examples: The insistent dog barked.
He was insistent.
An insistent knock came.

more.def: Firmly asking for something again and again.
examples: The insistent dog barked until we fed it.
He was insistent that we hurry.
An insistent knock on the door woke us.

easy.def: To look at something carefully.
examples: The doctor inspects my ears.
We inspect the bike.
She inspected the toy.

more.def: To look at something closely to check that it is good or safe.
examples: The mechanic inspected the bike for loose bolts.
The teacher inspected our work.
A worker inspects the bridge every year.

easy.def: A careful look to check something.
examples: The car needs an inspection.
The inspection was short.
The inspection found no problems.

more.def: A careful check to see that something is safe or correct.
examples: The car passed its yearly inspection.
The building inspection found no problems.
The teacher made an inspection of our desks.

easy.def: A person who checks that things are safe.
examples: The inspector checked the building.
The inspector looked at the bridge.
An inspector came to the school.

more.def: A person whose job is to look closely at something to see that it is safe or right.
examples: The inspector checked that the new bridge was safe.
A health inspector visited the restaurant kitchen.
The building inspector looked at the wiring.

easy.def: Something that gives you good ideas.
examples: Nature is her inspiration.
The story was an inspiration.
He found inspiration.

more.def: Something or someone that makes you want to do or make something good.
examples: Nature is the inspiration for her paintings.
Her teacher was an inspiration to the class.
The poem came from a flash of inspiration.

easy.def: Making you want to do good things.
examples: The story was inspirational.
Her speech was inspirational.
He is an inspirational teacher.

more.def: Giving you the feeling that you can do something good or great.
examples: The coach gave an inspirational talk before the game.
Her story of climbing the mountain was inspirational.
The poster had an inspirational message about trying again.

easy.def: To make someone want to do something good.
examples: The story inspired me.
The teacher inspires us.
Her kindness inspires me.

more.def: To make someone feel excited about doing something.
examples: The story of the brave girl inspired me to try.
The coach inspired the team to work hard.
Her kindness inspires everyone around her.

easy.def: To put in place so it works.
examples: Dad installed a new light.
We install the program.
They installed a new sink.

more.def: To put something in place and make it ready to use.
examples: Dad installed a new light in the kitchen.
The workers installed a new sink.
I installed the game on the computer.

easy.def: Putting something in place so that it can be used.
examples: The installation took an hour.
The installation of the new sink.
We watched the installation.

more.def: The act of putting equipment in place so that it is ready to use, or a place such as a base or a big art piece.
examples: The installation of the new computers took the whole morning.
Workers finished the installation of the playground swings.
The museum has an art installation made of hundreds of lights.

easy.def: An example of something.
examples: Give me an instance.
In this instance, we waited.
For instance, a dog is a pet.

more.def: One example of something that happens or exists.
examples: Can you give me an instance of a mammal?
In this instance, the bus was late.
Cats, for instance, like to sleep in warm places.

easy.def: A very short time.
examples: I will be there in an instant.
The light flashed for an instant.
In an instant, it was gone.

more.def: A very short moment.
examples: I will be back in an instant.
The lightning flashed for just an instant.
In an instant, the squirrel was up the tree.

easy.def: Happening or ready right away.
examples: I like instant oatmeal.
The pudding is instant.
It was an instant success.

more.def: Happening right away, or made to be ready in a short time.
examples: I eat instant oatmeal on busy mornings.
The magic trick was an instant hit.
Instant noodles are ready in three minutes.

easy.def: Right away.
examples: The light came on instantly.
She instantly knew the answer.
The cat ran off instantly.

more.def: Immediately, with no delay at all.
examples: The light came on instantly when I flipped the switch.
She instantly knew the answer to the riddle.
The puppy fell asleep instantly after its long walk.

easy.def: In place of something.
examples: I took an apple instead.
Let us walk instead.
She had tea instead of milk.

more.def: In place of something else.
examples: It was raining, so we played inside instead.
I wanted pizza, but we had soup instead.
He walked instead of taking the bus.

easy.def: Something an animal does without being taught.
examples: Birds fly by instinct.
A baby turtle goes to the sea by instinct.
The instinct is strong.

more.def: A natural way of acting that an animal or person is born with and does not have to learn.
examples: Baby turtles head for the sea by instinct.
A mother bird's instinct is to protect her eggs.
His instinct told him to step back.

easy.def: A place for study or special work.
examples: The institute teaches science.
She works at the institute.
An institute is a kind of school.

more.def: An organization or building that is set up for study, research or teaching.
examples: The science institute studies how plants grow.
She works at an institute that teaches art.
Scientists at the institute study the ocean.

easy.def: A big, important organization.
examples: A school is an institution.
The bank is an institution.
The museum is an institution.

more.def: A large, established organization such as a school, bank or hospital.
examples: A university is an institution that teaches many students.
The museum is a well-known institution in our city.
Banks and hospitals are institutions.

easy.def: To teach.
examples: The coach instructed the team.
I instruct my dog.
She instructs the class.

more.def: To teach someone a skill or to tell someone what to do.
examples: The coach instructed the team on how to pass.
The teacher instructed us to open our books.
She instructs the swimming class.

easy.def: Words that tell you how to do something.
examples: Follow the instructions.
Read the instruction.
The box has instructions.

more.def: A direction that tells you how to do something.
examples: Read the instructions before you build the model.
The teacher gave us clear instructions.
The instruction told us to stir slowly.

easy.def: Teaching.
examples: She gives swimming instruction.
The class received instruction in art.
He takes music instruction.

more.def: The act of teaching someone a skill or subject.
examples: She gives swimming instruction at the pool.
The students receive instruction in reading every day.
He took violin instruction on Saturdays.

easy.def: A person who teaches.
examples: The swim instructor is kind.
The instructor showed us.
The art instructor helped.

more.def: A person who teaches a skill or a subject.
examples: The swimming instructor showed us how to kick.
The instructor explained the rules.
Our art instructor helped us paint.

easy.def: A thing you play to make music.
examples: A drum is an instrument.
What instrument do you play?
A flute is an instrument you blow.

more.def: An object used to make music; also, a tool for careful work.
examples: The violin is her favorite instrument to play.
Every instrument in the band plays a different part.
The dentist used a small instrument to check my teeth.

easy.def: Playing an important part in something.
examples: She was instrumental in the win.
An instrumental song.
He was instrumental.

more.def: Playing an important part in making something happen, or having music without words.
examples: She was instrumental in organizing the school fair.
The band played an instrumental song with no singing.
His quick thinking was instrumental in saving the day.

easy.def: Not enough.
examples: The food was insufficient.
We have insufficient time.
The water was insufficient.

more.def: Not enough for what is needed.
examples: We had insufficient food for the whole class.
The light was insufficient to read by.
The money was insufficient to buy the toy.

easy.def: Stuff that keeps heat in or out.
examples: Insulation keeps the house warm.
The attic has insulation.
The wall has insulation.

more.def: A material that keeps heat, cold or sound from passing through.
examples: Insulation in the walls keeps the house warm in winter.
Pink insulation filled the attic.
A thick coat acts like insulation for your body.

easy.def: To say something mean to someone.
examples: Do not insult your friends.
He insulted me.
That insults her.

more.def: To say or do something rude that hurts someone's feelings.
examples: It is wrong to insult people.
He insulted her by laughing at her drawing.
She felt insulted when they ignored her.

easy.def: A rude thing said to hurt someone.
examples: That was an insult.
He gave an insult.
I did not like the insult.

more.def: Something rude said or done that hurts someone's feelings.
examples: Calling someone a name is an insult.
She took his words as an insult.
He apologized for his insult.

easy.def: Money you pay so that you get help if something bad happens.
examples: We have car insurance.
Insurance paid for the damage.
The house has insurance.

more.def: An agreement in which you pay money so that you will be paid if something bad happens.
examples: Dad pays for car insurance each month.
Insurance covered the cost of the repairs.
The family has insurance for their house.

easy.def: To pay money to be safe if something bad happens.
examples: Dad will insure the car.
They insured the house.
We insure our bikes.

more.def: To pay a company a small amount so it will pay for any loss or damage later.
examples: Mom bought a plan to insure the house against fire.
The family insured the car against accidents.
The musician insured her violin for a large amount.

easy.def: Whole and not broken.
examples: The vase is intact.
The egg is intact.
The box arrived intact.

more.def: Not broken, damaged or touched, still whole.
examples: The vase was still intact after the fall.
The package arrived intact.
The old castle walls were mostly intact.

easy.def: What you take in, like food or water.
examples: Your water intake matters.
Her intake of fruit grew.
The doctor checked his intake.

more.def: The amount of something, such as food, drink or air, that is taken into the body or a machine.
examples: Drinking water increases your daily intake of fluids.
The fan sucks air through the intake at the front.
A nurse wrote down the child's food intake.

easy.def: Doing what is right even when no one is watching.
examples: He has integrity.
She acted with integrity.
Integrity is important.

more.def: The quality of being honest and having strong rules about what is right.
examples: He is a person of integrity.
She showed integrity by telling the truth.
A good leader acts with integrity.

easy.def: The power of the mind to think and understand.
examples: She has a sharp intellect.
Puzzles help your intellect.
His intellect is strong.

more.def: The ability of the mind to think, reason and understand, especially in a deep and clear way.
examples: The scientist had a sharp intellect and solved hard problems.
Reading books helps to build your intellect.
His curious intellect made him ask big questions about space.

easy.def: Having to do with the mind.
examples: A chess game is intellectual.
An intellectual puzzle.
It is an intellectual job.

more.def: Having to do with thinking and learning.
examples: Chess is an intellectual game.
The puzzle was an intellectual challenge.
She enjoys intellectual talks.

easy.def: The ability to learn and think.
examples: Dolphins have great intelligence.
Her intelligence is clear.
Intelligence helps you solve problems.

more.def: The ability to learn, understand and think about things.
examples: Dolphins are known for their intelligence.
It takes intelligence to solve a hard puzzle.
Crows show great intelligence by using tools.

easy.def: Smart and able to learn.
examples: The dog is intelligent.
She is an intelligent girl.
Dolphins are intelligent.

more.def: Able to learn, understand and think about things well.
examples: Crows are intelligent birds that can solve puzzles.
She is an intelligent student who asks good questions.
The intelligent dog learned new tricks quickly.

easy.def: To plan to do something.
examples: I intend to go.
She intends to win.
He intended to call.

more.def: To have something in mind to do.
examples: I intend to finish my homework before dinner.
She intended to surprise her mother.
He intended to call but forgot.

easy.def: Very strong.
examples: The heat was intense.
The pain was intense.
She felt intense joy.

more.def: Very strong or very serious.
examples: The intense heat made us stay inside.
She watched the game with intense interest.
The pain was too intense to ignore.

easy.def: How strong something is.
examples: The intensity of the sun was high.
The intensity of the light hurt.
She played with intensity.

more.def: The strength or force of something, such as light, sound or feeling.
examples: The intensity of the sun was high at noon.
The intensity of the storm grew as night fell.
She played with great intensity in the last game.

easy.def: A plan or purpose.
examples: His intent was to help.
I had no bad intent.
The intent was kind.

more.def: What you mean to do, your purpose.
examples: His intent was to help his sister.
She had no bad intent when she laughed.
The intent of the rule is to keep us safe.

easy.def: What you plan to do.
examples: My intention is to help.
She had no intention of leaving.
It was my intention to be kind.

more.def: An idea or plan that you mean to carry out.
examples: My intention was to clean my room before dinner.
She had no intention of quitting.
He had good intentions, but he spilled the milk.

easy.def: Done on purpose.
examples: It was intentional.
An intentional move.
The mistake was intentional.

more.def: Done on purpose, not by accident.
examples: The spill was not intentional, so I said sorry.
It was an intentional move to confuse the other team.
The teacher knew the mistake was intentional.

easy.def: With full attention.
examples: She listened intently.
The cat watched the bird intently.
He read intently.

more.def: In a way that shows great attention and focus.
examples: She listened intently to the story.
The students listened intently to the guest speaker.
He studied the map intently.

easy.def: To talk and work with others.
examples: Kids interact at recess.
Dogs interact.
We interact with our friends.

more.def: To talk to, work with or affect each other.
examples: The children interact with each other at recess by playing games.
Zoo visitors can interact with the goats in the petting area.
Some medicines can interact and make you feel sick.

easy.def: When people or things act with each other.
examples: I had a nice interaction with the dog.
The children's interaction was kind.
We watched the interaction of the fish.

more.def: The way people or things act together and affect each other.
examples: The teacher watched the interaction between the two puppies.
Good interaction in a team helps everyone play better.
Scientists studied the interaction of bees and flowers.

easy.def: To stop something on its way.
examples: The player intercepted the ball.
The guard intercepted the note.
She intercepted the pass.

more.def: To catch or stop someone or something before it gets where it is going.
examples: The player intercepted the pass.
The teacher intercepted the note.
The goalie intercepted the shot.

easy.def: A system you use to talk to people in another room.
examples: The principal spoke on the intercom.
Use the intercom.
The intercom made a noise.

more.def: A system with microphones and speakers that lets people talk to each other in different rooms of a building.
examples: The principal spoke on the intercom to tell us the news.
We pressed the button on the intercom to talk to the front door.
The intercom crackled before the announcement.

easy.def: A wish to know more.
examples: She has an interest in space.
He lost interest.
He shows interest in bugs.

more.def: A feeling of wanting to learn about or take part in something.
examples: She has a big interest in dinosaurs.
He lost interest in the game.
My interest in music began at age five.

easy.def: Something you like to do.
examples: My interests are art and soccer.
Her interests include chess.
He has many interests.

more.def: Something that you enjoy doing or learning about.
examples: Her interests include painting and swimming.
Chess is one of his main interests.
We share an interest in birds.

easy.def: Wanting to know more.
examples: I am interested in space.
She was interested in the book.
He is interested in birds.

more.def: Wanting to learn about or take part in something.
examples: I am interested in learning to play the guitar.
She seemed interested in the bug on the leaf.
Are you interested in joining the choir?

easy.def: Making you want to know more.
examples: This is an interesting book.
The story is interesting.
I found an interesting bug.

more.def: Holding your attention and making you want to learn more.
examples: The museum had an interesting display of old coins.
That was the most interesting book I have read.
She told us an interesting fact about whales.

easy.def: To get in the way.
examples: Do not interfere.
The noise interferes with my reading.
The rain interfered with our picnic.

more.def: To get in the way of something or to step into a matter that is not yours.
examples: The noise interfered with my reading.
Loud music can interfere with studying.
Please do not interfere when I am helping my brother.

easy.def: Something that gets in the way and stops something from working well.
examples: There was interference on the radio.
Noise was interference.
The TV had bad interference.

more.def: Anything that gets in the way and stops something from working as it should.
examples: A storm caused interference with the radio signal.
The referee blew the whistle for interference during the game.
Our video call dropped because of interference on the line.

easy.def: The inside part.
examples: The interior of the house is warm.
The car's interior is clean.
The interior is blue.

more.def: The inside of something such as a building or car.
examples: The interior of the house was warm and bright.
The car's interior was clean.
We painted the interior of the barn.

easy.def: A short break in the middle of a show.
examples: We got a snack at intermission.
The play has an intermission.
Intermission is ten minutes.

more.def: A short break between parts of a show, such as a play or concert.
examples: We bought popcorn during the intermission.
The band took a rest at intermission.
Everyone stretched during the intermission of the long play.

easy.def: Inside.
examples: The internal parts of a clock are small.
The internal walls are thin.
The internal organs.

more.def: Found or happening inside something.
examples: The internal parts of the clock are tiny.
Your heart is an internal organ.
The internal walls of the house are painted white.

easy.def: Between or among countries.
examples: The games are international.
We went to an international fair.
She speaks an international language.

more.def: Involving two or more countries.
examples: The Olympics is an international event.
We went to an international food fair.
She is an international star known around the world.

easy.def: A huge network that connects computers all over the world.
examples: I look things up on the internet.
The internet is fast.
The internet connects people.

more.def: A huge system of computers all over the world that are linked together so people can share information.
examples: I looked up the answer on the internet.
The internet connects people around the world.
The school has fast internet.

easy.def: To tell what something means.
examples: She interprets the words for us.
I interpret the picture.
The guide interprets signs.

more.def: To explain what something means, or to understand it in a certain way.
examples: She interpreted the foreign words for us.
I interpreted the picture to be a happy moment.
The guide interpreted the old signs on the cave wall.

easy.def: What you think something means.
examples: Her interpretation of the story was funny.
That is my interpretation.
What is your interpretation?

more.def: The way you understand what something means, or the way a person performs or explains a piece of art or music.
examples: Everyone in the class had a different interpretation of the poem.
The singer's interpretation of the old song was slow and sweet.
Her interpretation of the dream was that she was worried about the test.

easy.def: A person who tells what someone is saying in another language.
examples: The interpreter helped us.
An interpreter spoke Spanish.
We needed an interpreter.

more.def: A person whose job is to say out loud in one language what someone has said in another language.
examples: The interpreter told us in English what the guide had said in French.
An interpreter helped the visitors talk to the doctor.
A sign-language interpreter stood beside the speaker.

easy.def: To stop someone when they are talking or busy.
examples: Please do not interrupt me.
Do not interrupt when I am on the phone.
The bell interrupted our game.

more.def: To stop someone while they are speaking or doing something.
examples: A loud knock interrupted the teacher in the middle of the story.
Sorry to interrupt, but dinner is ready.
A power cut interrupted the movie.

easy.def: Something that stops what you are doing for a short time.
examples: The phone call was an interruption.
Sorry for the interruption.
The noise was an interruption.

more.def: Something that makes a person or an activity stop for a short time.
examples: The loud siren outside was an interruption to our quiet reading time.
Sorry for the interruption, but I have a question.
After the power cut, the interruption lasted ten minutes.

easy.def: A place where two roads cross.
examples: Stop at the intersection.
The intersection is busy.
We crossed at the intersection.

more.def: A place where two or more roads meet or cross, or the point where two lines cross.
examples: Stop and look both ways at the intersection before you cross.
The traffic light at the intersection turned green.
The two lines meet at an intersection on the graph.

easy.def: A big road that goes between states.
examples: We drove on the interstate.
The interstate is fast.
The interstate is busy.

more.def: A very wide, fast road with several lanes that goes between states.
examples: We drove on the interstate for six hours to reach the beach.
The interstate was busy with trucks and cars.
Exit signs line the interstate every few miles.

easy.def: A time or space between two things.
examples: There was an interval between songs.
A short interval.
The interval was ten minutes.

more.def: A period of time or a space between two events or things.
examples: There was a short interval between the two songs.
The buses run at ten-minute intervals.
Plant the seeds at regular intervals along the row.

easy.def: To step in to stop or help with a problem.
examples: The teacher intervened.
A grown-up must intervene.
She intervened in the argument.

more.def: To step in to help or to change what is happening, especially to stop a problem or a fight.
examples: The teacher intervened when two students began arguing over the ball.
A lifeguard intervened and helped the tired swimmer out of the water.
Mom intervened and found a fair way to share the toy.

easy.def: A talk where someone asks questions.
examples: The reporter did an interview.
Mom had a job interview.
The interview was short.

more.def: A meeting in which someone asks a person questions.
examples: The reporter did an interview with the winner.
Mom has a job interview on Monday.
The interview was on the radio.

easy.def: To ask someone questions.
examples: I interviewed my grandpa.
She interviews the winner.
He interviewed the mayor.

more.def: To ask someone questions in order to learn about them.
examples: I interviewed my grandfather for a school project.
The reporter interviewed the winner.
She interviews people for a magazine.

easy.def: A long tube in your body that helps digest food.
examples: Food goes into the intestine.
The intestine is long.
Your intestine helps you digest.

more.def: A long, twisting tube in the body that digests food after it leaves the stomach and takes in what the body needs.
examples: Food moves from the stomach into the intestine, where the body takes in what it needs.
The small intestine is very long and folded up inside your belly.
A healthy intestine helps your body use the food you eat.

easy.def: To make someone feel scared or afraid.
examples: The big dog may intimidate you.
I felt intimidated by the tall boy.
The high wall intimidated me.

more.def: To make someone feel afraid or less confident, often by being big or strong.
examples: The large dog intimidated the little kids.
I felt intimidated by the tall wall.
The big class intimidated the new student at first.

easy.def: Scary because it seems big or strong.
examples: The big dog looks intimidating.
The tall wall was intimidating.
The test seemed intimidating.

more.def: Making you feel afraid or nervous because of size, power or difficulty.
examples: The huge, growling dog looked intimidating.
Standing on the big stage felt intimidating.
The tall mountain looked intimidating to the new climbers.

easy.def: A word that shows going to the inside.
examples: The cat jumped into the box.
We walked into the room.
Put the toys into the bin.

more.def: A word used to show movement to the inside of something, or a change to another form.
examples: The frog leaped into the pond with a splash.
A caterpillar turns into a butterfly.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake it.

easy.def: Not willing to accept people or ideas that are different.
examples: An intolerant person is unfair.
He was intolerant of noise.
Do not be intolerant.

more.def: Not willing to accept people or ideas that are different from your own.
examples: An intolerant person does not listen to other views.
He was intolerant of noise when he studied.
The class talked about how not to be intolerant.

easy.def: Having many small, fine parts.
examples: The lace has an intricate pattern.
He drew an intricate picture.
An intricate web hung in the tree.

more.def: Having many small, detailed parts that are carefully arranged or hard to understand.
examples: The spider spun an intricate web between the two branches.
She wore a dress with an intricate pattern of tiny flowers.
The clock had an intricate machine of gears inside.

easy.def: To make someone very interested.
examples: The puzzle intrigues me.
The old map intrigued us.
The story intrigued her.

more.def: To make someone very curious or interested, so that they want to know more.
examples: The strange old box intrigued the children.
The mystery of the missing shoes intrigued me.
The story's first line intrigued her and made her read on.

easy.def: Secret plans and mysterious happenings.
examples: The story is full of intrigue.
A tale of intrigue.
Intrigue filled the palace.

more.def: Secret plans and mysterious events, especially in a story or at a palace.
examples: The novel is a tale of intrigue and secret plans in the palace.
The spy story was full of intrigue.
Whispers of intrigue filled the castle halls.

easy.def: Strange and interesting, so you want to know more.
examples: It was an intriguing story.
An intriguing box.
The smell was intriguing.

more.def: Very interesting because it is strange or mysterious and makes you want to know more.
examples: The old map was intriguing, and we wanted to find where the X was.
It was an intriguing puzzle with no clear answer.
The detective found an intriguing clue under the rug.

easy.def: To tell people each other's names.
examples: Let me introduce my friend.
She introduced me to her mom.
He introduced himself.

more.def: To tell people each other's names when they meet for the first time.
examples: Let me introduce you to my cousin.
The teacher introduced the new student to the class.
He introduced himself to the neighbors.

easy.def: When you tell people who someone is.
examples: Let me make an introduction.
The introduction was short.
I made an introduction.

more.def: The act of presenting someone to another person, or the first part of a book or talk.
examples: Let me make an introduction between my friends.
The introduction to the book was short.
The teacher gave an introduction to the new student.

easy.def: To go in where you are not wanted.
examples: I do not want to intrude.
Please do not intrude on my room.
The cat intruded on our picnic.

more.def: To come into a place or a talk where you are not invited or wanted.
examples: I hope I am not intruding on your game.
A raccoon intruded into our camp and ate our snacks.
She did not want to intrude on their private talk.

easy.def: A person who goes where they are not welcome.
examples: The dog barked at the intruder.
An intruder was in the yard.
The alarm scared the intruder.

more.def: A person who enters a place without permission.
examples: The security camera caught the intruder.
The alarm went off when the intruder came in.
An intruder was found in the garden.

easy.def: Coming in where you are not wanted.
examples: I am sorry for the intrusion.
The noise was an intrusion.
The intrusion upset us.

more.def: The act of coming into a place or a situation where you are not wanted or invited.
examples: I am sorry for the intrusion, but I need to ask a quick question.
The loud noise was an intrusion into our quiet afternoon.
The neighbors disliked the intrusion of the loud music.

easy.def: A feeling that you know something without being told.
examples: I had an intuition.
My intuition was right.
She trusts her intuition.

more.def: A feeling that something is true without needing proof.
examples: I had an intuition that it would rain, and it did.
Her intuition told her that her friend was sad.
He followed his intuition and went left.

easy.def: To enter a place to take it over.
examples: The army invaded the land.
Ants invaded the kitchen.
Weeds invaded the garden.

more.def: To enter a place by force, or to spread into a place where you are not wanted.
examples: The army invaded the neighboring land.
Tiny bugs invaded the picnic table.
Rabbits invaded the vegetable patch and ate the lettuce.

related.def: A person or thing that invades.

easy.def: Not good or not allowed.
examples: The ticket is invalid.
An invalid answer.
Your card is invalid.

more.def: Not accepted or not correct, because it does not follow the rules or is no longer good to use.
examples: The ticket was invalid because it had expired.
The computer said my password was invalid.
The answer was invalid because it did not follow the directions.

easy.def: When an army enters a country to take it over.
examples: The invasion began at dawn.
The people feared an invasion.
The invasion was stopped.

more.def: The act of entering a place by force in order to take it over.
examples: The invasion of the castle began at dawn.
Ants carried out an invasion of the kitchen.
The people feared the invasion of their land.

easy.def: To make something that no one has made before.
examples: I want to invent a robot that cleans my room.
She invented a new game.
Who invented the bike?

more.def: To think of and create something new for the first time.
examples: People invented the wheel thousands of years ago.
He invented a machine that feeds the cat.
The children invented a secret code for their notes.

related.def: To make something again in a new way.

easy.def: Something new that someone made.
examples: The light bulb was a great invention.
I made an invention.
The invention helps people.

more.def: A new thing that someone has made or thought of for the first time.
examples: The printing press was an important invention.
She showed her class an invention that waters plants.
The invention of the wheel changed the world.

easy.def: Good at thinking up new things.
examples: He is inventive.
An inventive girl made a toy.
The inventive cook made a new dish.

more.def: Good at thinking up new ideas and ways of doing things.
examples: The inventive girl built a robot from junk.
He is an inventive cook who tries new dishes.
An inventive plan saved the day.

easy.def: A person who thinks up and makes new things.
examples: The inventor made a new toy.
She is an inventor.
The inventor built a robot.

more.def: A person who thinks up and makes something that did not exist before.
examples: The inventor built a machine that could sort socks by color.
Many inventors worked on the first airplane before one finally flew.
My sister wants to be an inventor when she grows up.

easy.def: To put money into something to make more money.
examples: Dad invests money.
She invested her savings.
He invested in a farm.

more.def: To put money or time into something hoping it will grow or pay off.
examples: Dad invested some money in a small business.
She invested her savings in a new bike shop.
I invest time in practice to get better.

easy.def: To look for facts to learn what happened.
examples: The detective will investigate.
We investigate the strange noise.
Police investigated.

more.def: To look carefully for facts in order to find out the truth.
examples: The class investigated why the plant died.
The police investigated the lost bike.
Scientists investigate how animals find their way home.

easy.def: Looking carefully to find out the facts.
examples: The police began an investigation.
The investigation took days.
A careful investigation.

more.def: A careful search to find out the facts about something.
examples: The police began an investigation of the lost bike.
Scientists carried out an investigation of the old tree.
The investigation took three days.

easy.def: Looking closely to find out the facts.
examples: An investigative reporter.
Investigative work.
An investigative mind.

more.def: Looking into something very carefully to find out the facts.
examples: The investigative reporter spent weeks finding out the facts about the story.
The detective did some investigative work to solve the mystery.
Scientists use investigative methods to learn about nature.

easy.def: A person who looks for facts about something.
examples: The investigator looked for clues.
An investigator came.
The investigator took notes.

more.def: A person whose job is to find out the facts about something.
examples: The investigator looked for clues at the scene.
A fire investigator found the cause.
The investigator wrote down every detail.

easy.def: A person who puts money into something to try to make more money.
examples: The investor gave money to the new shop.
An investor bought shares.
My aunt is an investor.

more.def: A person who puts money into a business or other plan hoping to make more money.
examples: An investor gave money to help the small bakery grow.
Investors bought shares in the new company.
My uncle is an investor who buys part of new businesses.

easy.def: Too strong to be beaten.
examples: The hero felt invincible.
The team was invincible.
He thought he was invincible.

more.def: So strong or powerful that nothing can beat or harm it.
examples: The champion team was invincible and won every game of the season.
The superhero in the cartoon is invincible, but real people need helmets.
The castle seemed invincible behind its thick stone walls.

easy.def: Not able to be seen.
examples: The air is invisible.
The ghost was invisible.
An invisible friend.

more.def: Impossible to see.
examples: Air is invisible, but we can feel the wind.
The hero in the story wore a cloak that made him invisible.
Tiny germs are invisible to the eye.

easy.def: A note asking you to come to something.
examples: I got an invitation to a party.
The invitation says to come at two.
She wrote the invitation.

more.def: A message that asks someone to come to a party or event.
examples: I got an invitation to her birthday party.
The invitation said to come at two o'clock.
He made an invitation with paper and markers.

easy.def: To ask someone to come.
examples: I will invite my friends to my party.
Our teacher invited a vet to class.
Invite your sister to play.

more.def: To ask someone to come somewhere or to do something with you.
examples: We invited our new neighbors over for dinner.
The neighbors invited us to their barbecue.
She was invited to speak at the meeting.

easy.def: To have something as a part.
examples: The game involves running.
Baking involves measuring.
This job involves lots of walking.

more.def: To include something as a necessary part.
examples: Playing the piano involves a lot of practice.
The project involves building a model volcano.
Camping involves sleeping in a tent.

easy.def: Being part of something.
examples: Her involvement helped.
I thank you for your involvement.
The club needs involvement.

more.def: The act of taking part in something.
examples: Her involvement made the project a success.
Parents' involvement helps the school.
The club needs everyone's involvement.

easy.def: Toward the inside.
examples: The door opens inward.
Look inward.
Fold the paper inward.

more.def: Toward the inside or the middle.
examples: The bridge slopes inward at the middle.
Fold the corners of the paper inward.
The gate swung inward.
